This chart retains 28 admitted star placements. Qi Sha in Life offers one entry through decisive cutting, high-pressure choice and directional action; Tian Liang in Siblings introduces the different function of protection, standards, oversight and repair. The following chapters select material by domain rather than turning every placement into one personality label.

The twelve palaces form six opposite axes, with triad and adjacent-palace relationships. These are structural coordinates: opposition is not automatically conflict, and a triad is not automatically support. Interpretation requires the relevant functions, conditions and counter-expressions as well.

Read from core orientation and inner experience into work, resources, relationships and support. Long cycles and current timing have their own chapters, followed by navigation. This separates the conditions present in the natal structure from the domains foregrounded at a particular time.

pages.title: Chart Architecture
items: Locate Life and Body separately
Twelve palaces and six opposite axes
Locate placements before interpreting context

paragraphs.text: The twelve natal palaces separate domains of experience. The Life Palace occupies the ZI branch; Body is located in Spouse. Read Life and the domain containing Body together; Body is not a thirteenth independent palace.

This chart retains 28 admitted star placements. Qi Sha in Life offers one entry through decisive cutting, high-pressure choice and directional action; Tian Liang in Siblings introduces the different function of protection, standards, oversight and repair. The following chapters select material by domain rather than turning every placement into one personality label.

The twelve palaces form six opposite axes, with triad and adjacent-palace relationships. These are structural coordinates: opposition is not automatically conflict, and a triad is not automatically support. Interpretation requires the relevant functions, conditions and counter-expressions as well.

Read from core orientation and inner experience into work, resources, relationships and support. Long cycles and current timing have their own chapters, followed by navigation. This separates the conditions present in the natal structure from the domains foregrounded at a particular time.

Distinguish choosing to step back from being pushed back by pressure. pages.title: Resources & Wealth
items: Tan Lang · Wealth
exploration constrained by clear priorities and limits
dispersion, excess appetite or commitments outrunning capacity

paragraphs.text: Acquiring resources and retaining them are different questions. Tan Lang in Wealth describes direction through “draw resources toward growth, access and optionality”; Wen Qu in Property brings in “use aesthetic, linguistic or symbolic assets to create value”. Property evidence does not promise real-estate ownership; it helps examine the conditions under which an arrangement can persist.

For acquisition, read “decide by comparing opportunity, interest and trade-offs” alongside the actual terms of exchange. An attractive opening does not establish a clear net return. Make visible who supplies time, funding or support, and what form the return would take.

For allocation, ask not only where resources could go next, but which capacities are already committed. nuanced expression anchored to observable context offers a holding condition in Property. If Wealth moves toward dispersion, excess appetite or commitments outrunning capacity, additional commitments may crowd out capacity that needed to remain available.

Separate retention from ownership: access is not ownership, and an amount recorded is not necessarily freely deployable. The Property decision pattern, “decide by sensing tone, symbolism and interpretive fit”, prompts a check of authorization, handoff, records and dependencies. Those are questions for real-world verification, not legal rights inferred from a star.

Optionality need not mean adding more options. Reducing overlapping demands or keeping an unresolved commitment reversible may better support exploration constrained by clear priorities and limits. If holding conditions narrow toward ambiguity, impression management or meaning detached from facts, re-examine the arrangement rather than treating further commitment as the only answer.

Test this chapter against a resource record: what came in, where it was allocated, what remained, who held decision rights and how much room was still uncommitted. Timing changes the focus of observation; it neither guarantees returns nor replaces actual financial information.

paragraphs.text: Tian Xiang brings seek reciprocity, proportion and workable mediation into relating, while co-present Zi Wei adds central coordination and stewardship. Coordination therefore concerns who sets priorities, distributes responsibility and leaves room for the other person, not merely whether agreement is reached.

Di Jie brings the expected continuity of an arrangement back under examination: “stress-test retention, transfer and dependency assumptions”. This is not a verdict of inevitable relationship loss. It asks whether continuity, support and dependency have actually been confirmed; realistic release and reallocation without catastrophe framing leaves room for adjustment.

Body also occupies Spouse, making position and choice in interaction a relevant practical setting. In the surrounding network, Ju Men offers relate through dialogue, naming differences and negotiating meaning as a counter-condition. If this becomes chronic disputation, mistrust or fixation on what is wrong, more explanation need not mean more understanding. Distinguish unresolved differences from repeated reactions.

A workable arrangement leaves room for fair coordination that still permits judgment while making visible when bureaucratic rigidity, people-pleasing or role confusion appears. Check who can propose change, who can decline and which commitments can be renegotiated. The chart cannot state another person's intentions or promise a marriage outcome.

paragraphs.text: Support is more than someone offering help. You Bi in Parents supplies a relational lens through offer tactful, responsive assistance without taking over. Tian Liang in Siblings brings “choose by durability, standards and downstream consequences” into peer coordination. Number of contacts, willingness to ask and help that is actually available are distinct observations.
